subject: Request: Zero-Trust IAM Artifacts — SCIM deletion logs & RBAC mapping
messages:
From: Greenline Health Compliance <compliance@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Security <security@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence request — SCIM deletion logs, SAML samples, RBAC mapping for SOC 2 readiness

Hi Vivek,

As part of Greenline's SOC 2 audit (scheduled for mid-December) our auditors have asked for a tight packet of IAM artifacts covering the period 2026-08-01 to 2026-11-24. Specifically we need:

- SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning events (deletion timestamps and affected user IDs)
- Sample SAML assertions for a successful and a failed login (including timestamps and assertion IDs)
- An RBAC role-to-permission mapping for all production roles active in that window
- Service account inventory and owner attestations for any accounts with wide privileges

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide raw SCIM deletion logs and a role mapping export by next Wednesday (2026-11-30)? The auditors prefer raw CSV/JSON exports — they will ingest them directly.

Please let us know if we should expect any PII redaction or if a filtered export is required. If helpful we can provide the exact field list auditors want.

Thanks,

Lina Park
Compliance Manager, Greenline Health
compliance@greenlinehealth.com

——
Greenline Health is collecting this under our audit intake. Please reply-all so Security and Compliance stay aligned.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Greenline Health Compliance <compliance@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — SCIM deletion logs, SAML samples, RBAC mapping for SOC 2 readiness

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. We're able to deliver the artifacts but have a couple of clarifying questions to make sure we match the auditor ingestion schema: 

1) Time window: you asked through 2026-11-24 — do you want us to include the full day (up to 23:59:59) or stop at the end of business (UTC 00:00)?
2) SCIM deletions: should we include only user-type deletions (users and service accounts) or also groups and entitlements?
3) RBAC mapping: auditors often want both role -> permission and permission -> role reverse mapping (two sheets). Confirm preference.

Monica and Aditya — can you take point on generating the exports? Monica, please prepare the RBAC workbook and owner attestations. Aditya, please pull the SCIM deletion export and a sample of SAML assertions (one accepted, one rejected).

We will plan to send a secure Drive link and attach small CSV samples in email; larger artifacts will be shared via a pre-approved intake link.

Vivek
Director, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Health Compliance <compliance@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — SCIM deletion logs, SAML samples, RBAC mapping for SOC 2 readiness

Vivek / Lina / Aditya — quick status update and plan: 

- SCIM deletions: Aditya exported the tenant-level deletion log for 2026-08-01 through 2026-11-24 (inclusive to 23:59:59 UTC). File: scim_deletion_log_202611.csv (attached). The CSV includes: timestamp_utc, actor_id, target_id, change_type, resource_type, note. We redacted email addresses in the note column per PII policy; auditors asked for hashes, we included SHA256 digests in the note column.

- SAML samples: attached saml_assertions_sample.txt with two assertions (one success, one failure), assertion IDs, and timestamps. We removed user session cookies and full attributes that contain phone numbers.

- RBAC mapping: rbac_role_mapping_2026-11.xlsx (attached) contains two sheets: Role->Permissions and Permission->Roles. We also included a short sheet that lists active role owners and last owner attestation date.

- Service account inventory: inventory file is large; we exported a stub file service_account_inventory_202611.json-stub.txt and uploaded the full JSON to our secure drive (link below). Each service account record includes owner, creation_ts, last_used_ts, and permissions. We flagged 7 accounts with owner missing — we recommend owner attestation for those.

Link to secure intake folder: https://redwood.app/drive/GLH/SCIM-deletions-202611
DocuSign link for owner attestations: https://docusign.com/req/GLH-ack-20261130

Next steps: Lina, if auditors want the full JSON inventory we can provision a temporary S3 download link with expiration. Also, please confirm if hashed emails are acceptable for your ingestion; if not we will produce a redacted but reversible tokenization export under NDA.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Security Analyst, Redwood Inference

Attachments: scim_deletion_log_202611.csv (CSV), saml_assertions_sample.txt (TXT), rbac_role_mapping_2026-11.xlsx (XLSX), service_account_inventory_202611.json-stub.txt (TXT)

From: Greenline Health Security <security@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — SCIM deletion logs, SAML samples, RBAC mapping for SOC 2 readiness

Monica / Vivek — thanks for the quick turnaround and comprehensive packet. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- Hashing of emails is acceptable for the SCIM CSV, auditors have confirmed they can match on the SHA256 digest.
- The SAML assertion sample is sufficient — can you also include the certificate thumbprint used by your IdP in the assertion header if available?
- We'll need the full service account inventory JSON (not the stub) behind a time-limited link. Please provision with a pre-signed URL that expires in 7 days and enable object-level logging in the bucket.

We'll sign the owner attestation DocuSign envelope today. Once signed we'll confirm and the auditors will proceed to ingest. If anything else comes up we will ping this thread.

Best,
Tom Alvarez
Head of Security, Greenline Health
security@greenlinehealth.com
